verses.sanskrit:
जनमेजय उवाच।
              यज्ञे सक्ता नृपतयस्तपःसक्ता महर्षयः। शान्तिव्यवस्थिता विप्राः शमे दम इति प्रभो॥१॥
तस्माद्यज्ञफलैस्तुल्यं न किञ्चिदिह दृश्यते। इति मे वर्तते बुद्धिस्तथा चैतदसंशयम्॥२॥
verses.bhavadeepa: यज्ञे सक्ता नृपतय इत्यध्यायो हिंसामिश्रस्वधर्मस्य निन्दार्थम्॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा तु बहवो राजानो द्विजसत्तमाः। इह कीर्तिं परां प्राप्य प्रेत्य स्वर्गमवाप्नुयुः॥३॥
verses.english: Numberless kings, O best of twice-born persons, having adored the celestials in sacrifices, acquired high fame here and obtained the celestial region hercafter.

verses.sanskrit: देवराजः सहस्राक्षः क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः। देवराज्यं महातेजाः प्राप्तवानखिलं विभुः॥४॥
verses.english: Gifted with great energy, the powerful king of the deities, viz., Indra of a thousand eyes, obtained the sovereignty over the deities through the many sacrifices he performed with gifts in profusion and attained to the fruition of all his desires.

verses.sanskrit: यदा युधिष्ठिरो राजा भीमार्जुन पुरःसरः। सदृशो देवराजेन समृद्ध्या विक्रमेण च॥५॥
verses.english: When king Yudhishthira, with Bhima and Arjuna by him, resembled the king of the deities himself in prosperity and prowess, why then did that mungoose depreciate that great Horse-Sacrifice of the great monarch.

verses.sanskrit: अथ कस्मात्स नकुलो गर्हयामास तं क्रतुम्। अश्वमेधं महायज्ञं राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः॥६॥

वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              यज्ञस्य विधिमग्र्यं वै फलं चापि नराधिप। गदतः शृणु मे राजन्यथावदिह भारत॥७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Do you listen to me, O king, as I describe to you duly, O Bharata, the excellent ordinances about sacrifice and the fruits also, O king, that sacrifice yields.

verses.sanskrit: पुरा शक्रस्य यजतः सर्व ऊचुर्महर्षयः। ऋत्विक्षु कर्मव्यग्रेषु वितते यज्ञकर्मणि॥८॥
verses.english: Formerly, occasion Shakra celebrated a particular sacrifice. While the limbs of the sacrifice were spread out, the Ritvijas became busy in performing the various rites ordained in the scriptures.

verses.sanskrit: हूयमाने तथा वह्नौ होत्रे गुणसमन्विते। देवेष्वाहूयमानेषु स्थितेषु परमर्षिषु॥९॥
verses.english: The pourer of libations, possessed of every qualification, becaine engaged in pouring libations of clarified butter. The great Rishis were seated around. The celestials were summoned by one by contented Brahmanas of great learning uttering scriptural Mantras in sweet voices. Those foremost of Adhvaryyus, not fatigued with what they did, recited the Mantras of the Yajurveda in soft account. on one one

verses.sanskrit: सुप्रतीतैस्तथा विप्रैः स्वागमैः सुस्वरैर्नृप। अश्रान्तैश्चापि लघुभिरध्वर्युवृषभैस्तथा॥१०॥
आलम्भसमये तस्मिन् गृहीतेषु पशुष्वथ। महर्षयो महाराज बभूवुः कृपयान्विताः॥११॥
verses.english: The time came for killing the animals. When the animals selected for sacrifice were seized, the great Rishis, O king, felt mercy for them.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दीनान्पशून्दृष्ट्वा ऋषयस्ते तपोधनाः। ऊचुः शक्रं समागम्य नायं यज्ञविधिः शुभः॥१२॥
verses.english: Seeing that the animals had all become dispirited, those Rishis, gifted with wealth of penances, approached Shakra and said to him, “This method of sacrifice is not auspicious.'

verses.sanskrit: अपरिज्ञानमेतत्ते महान्तं धर्ममिच्छतः। न हि यज्ञे पशुगण विधिदृष्टाः पुरन्दर॥१३॥
verses.english: Desirous of winning great merit as you are, this is, indeed, a mark of your ignorance of the rites of sacrifice. O Purandara, animals have not been ordained to be killed in sacrifices,

verses.sanskrit: धर्मोपघातकस्त्वेष समारम्भस्तव प्रभो। नायं धर्मकृतो यज्ञो न हिंसा धर्म उच्यते॥१४॥
verses.english: O powerful one, these preparations of yours are destructive of merit! This sacrifice is not consistent with virtue. The destruction of creatures can never be said to be an act of virtue!

verses.sanskrit: आगमेनैव ते यज्ञं कुर्वन्तु यदि चेच्छसि॥१५॥
verses.english: If you wish it, let your priests perform your sacrifice according to the Agama. By performing a sacrifice according to the scriptural ordinance, great will be the merit acquired by you.

verses.sanskrit: विधिदृष्टेन यज्ञेन धर्मस्ते सुमहान्भवेत्। यज बीजैः सहस्राक्ष त्रिवर्षपरमोषितैः॥१६॥
एष धर्मो महान् शक्र महागुणफलोदयः। शतक्रतुस्तु तद्वाक्यमृषिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः॥१७॥
verses.english: you of a hundred eyes do you perform the sacrifice with seeds of grain which have been kept for three years. This, O Shakra, would be fraught with great virtue and productive of fruits of high efficacy.

verses.sanskrit: उक्तं न प्रतिजग्राह मानान्मोहवशं गतः। तेषां विवादः सुमहान् शक्रयज्ञे तपस्विनाम्॥१८॥
verses.english: were The deity of a hundred sacrifices, however, moved by pride and overwhelmed by stupefaction, did not accept these words uttered by the Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: जङ्गमैः स्थावरैर्वापि यष्टव्यमिति भारत। ते तु खिन्ना विवादेन ऋषयस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः॥१९॥
verses.english: Then, O Bharata, a great dispute arose in that sacrifice of Shakra between the ascetics as to how sacrifices should be performed, that is, should they be performed, with mobile creatures or with immobile objects.

verses.sanskrit: तदा सन्धाय शक्रेण पप्रच्छर्नृपतिं वसुम्। धर्मसंशयमापन्नान्सत्यं ब्रूहि महामते॥२०॥
verses.english: All of them exhausted with disputation. The Rishis, then, those beholders of truth, having made a compact with Shakra, asked king Vasu.

verses.sanskrit: महाभाग कथं यज्ञेष्वागमो नृपसत्तम। यष्टव्यं पशुभिर्मुख्यैरथो बीजै रसैरिति॥२१॥
verses.english: O highly blessed one, what is the Vedic declaration about sacrifices? Is it preferable to perform sacrifices with animals or with seeds and juices.

verses.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा तु वसुस्तेषामविचार्य बलाबलम्। यथोपनीतैर्यष्टव्यमिति प्रोवाच पार्थिवः॥२२॥
verses.english: Hearing the question, king Vasu, without at all judging the merits of the arguments advanced on both sides, at once answered, saying, 'Sacrifices may be performed with any of the two kinds of objects ready.'

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा स नृपतिः प्रविवेश रसातलम्। उक्त्वाथ वितथं प्रश्नं चेदीनामीश्वरः प्रभुः॥२३॥
verses.english: Having answered the question thus, he had to enter the nether regions. Indeed, the powerful king of the Chedis had to undergo that misery for having answered falsely.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मान्न वाच्यं ह्येकेन बहुज्ञेनापि संशये। प्रजापतिमपाहाय स्वयम्भुवमृते प्रभुम्॥२४॥
verses.english: Therefore, when a doubt arises, no person, however wise, should singly decide the matter, unless he be the powerful and self-born Lord himself of creatures,

verses.sanskrit: तेन दत्तानि दानानि पापेनाशुद्धबुद्धिना। तानि सर्वानादृत्य नश्यन्ति विपुलान्यपि॥२५॥
verses.english: Gifts made by a sinner with an impure heart, for this, when very large, become lost. Such gifts go for nothing.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याधर्मप्रवृत्तस्य हिंसकस्य दुरात्मनः। दानेन कीर्तिर्भवति न प्रेत्येह च दुर्मतेः॥२६॥
verses.english: By the gifts made by a person of unrighteous conduct, one, that is, who is of sinful soul and who is a destroyer, just fame never acquired either in this world or in the next.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यायोपगतं द्रव्यमभीक्ष्णं यो हपण्डितः। धर्माभिशङ्की यजते न स धर्मफलं लभेत्॥२७॥
verses.english: That person of little intelligence, who, from desire of acquiring merit, celebrates sacrifices with wealth acquired by unfair means, never succeeds in acquiring merit.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मवैतंसिको यस्तु पापात्मा पुरुषाधमः। ददाति दानं विप्रेभ्यो लोकविश्वासकारणम्॥२८॥
verses.english: That low wretch of sin who hypocritically assuming a garb of virtue makes gifts to Brahmanas, only created the conviction in men about his own virtue.

verses.sanskrit: पापेन कर्मणा विप्रो धनं प्राप्य निरङ्कुशः। रागमोहान्वितः सोऽन्ते कलुषां गतिमश्नुते॥२९॥
verses.english: That Brahmana of uncontrolled conduct, who acquires wealth by sinful deeds, overwhelmed by passion and stupefaction, attains at last to the goal of the sinful.

verses.sanskrit: अपि सञ्चयबुद्धिर्हि लोभमोहवशङ्गतः। उद्वेजयति भूतानि पापेनाशुद्धबुद्धिना॥३०॥
verses.english: Some one, overwhelmed by cupidity and stupefaction, becomes bent on storing riches. He is seen to persecute all creatures, urged by a sinful and impure understanding.

verses.sanskrit: एवं लब्ध्वा धनं मोहाद्यो हि दद्याद्यजेत वा। न तस्य स फलं प्रेत्य भुङ्क्ते पापधनागमात्॥३१॥
verses.english: He who, having acquired riches by such means, makes gifts or performs sacrifices therewith, never enjoys the fruits of those gifts or sacrifices in the other world on account of the wealth having been acquired by unfair means.

verses.sanskrit: उञ्छं मूलं फलं शाकमुदपात्रं तपोधनाः। दानं विभवतो दत्वा नराः स्वर्यान्ति धार्मिकाः॥३२॥
एष धर्मो महायोगो दानं भूतदया तथा। ब्रह्मचर्यं तथा सत्यमनुक्रोशो धृतिः क्षमा॥३३॥
सनातनस्य धर्मस्य मूलमेतत्सनातनम्। श्रूयन्ते हि पुरा वृत्ता विश्वामित्रादयो नृपाः॥३४॥
verses.english: Such gifts are fraught with virtue and equal to high austerities. Such gifts, as also mercy to all creatures, and Brahmacharya, truthfulness of speech, and kindness, and fortitude, and forgiveness, form the eternal foundations of virtue which itself is eternal. We hear of Vishvamitra and other kings of ancient times.

verses.sanskrit: विश्वामित्रोऽसितश्चैव जनकश्च महीपति। कक्षसेनार्ष्टिसेनौ च सिन्धुद्वीपश्च पार्थिवः॥३५॥
verses.english: Indeed, Vishmvamitra, and Asita, and king Janaka, and Kakshasena and Arshtisena and king Sindhudvipa, these and many other kings, gifted with wealth of penances, having made gifts of articles acquired by fairness, having attained to high success.

verses.sanskrit: एते चान्ये च बहवः सिद्धिं परमिकां गताः। नृपाः सत्यैश्च दानैश्च न्यायलब्धैस्तपोधनाः॥३६॥
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्रा ये चाश्रितास्तपः। दानधर्माग्निना शुद्धास्ते स्वर्गं यान्ति भारत॥३७॥
